name: PYTHON_SCRIPT
description: Executes Python code or a Python script. Input and output data are exchanged as JSON objects with type information.

parameters.name: pythonCode
parameters.description: A string containing the Python code to execute. Mutually exclusive with 'scriptPath'.

parameters.name: scriptPath
parameters.description: URI (e.g., 'file:/path/to/your/script.py') of the Python script to execute. Mutually exclusive with 'pythonCode'.

parameters.name: inputVariables
parameters.description: A map where keys are names of variables in the input 'Data' object, and values are the corresponding variable names to be created in the Python script's global scope. Example: {'data_input_key': 'python_var_x'}

parameters.name: outputVariables
parameters.description: A map where keys are Python variable names in the script's global scope whose values should be captured, and values are the corresponding keys under which they will be stored in the output 'Data' object. Example: {'python_result_var': 'data_output_key'}

parameters.name: pythonPath
parameters.description: Optional path to a specific Python executable (e.g., '/usr/bin/python3.8' or 'path/to/venv/bin/python'). If not set, tries 'python3' then 'python' from PATH.

parameters.name: setupCode
parameters.description: Optional Python code string that will be executed once during the initialization of the Python environment for this step (e.g., for imports or global setup). This code runs before the main 'pythonCode' or 'scriptPath'.

parameters.name: returnFullPythonGlobals
parameters.description: If true, all non-builtin global variables from the Python script's execution scope will be returned in the output Data object (keys will be Python variable names). Overrides 'outputVariables' if true. Defaults to false.

parameters.name: args
parameters.description: A list of string arguments to be passed to the Python script if 'scriptPath' is used (sys.argv).

parameters.name: environmentVariables
parameters.description: A map of environment variables (key-value strings) to set for the Python process. Note: Direct support depends on execution method; current Apache Commons Exec has limited direct support.
